explanation: The V82F mutation introduces a bulky aromatic side chain that creates steric interference with indinavir's binding geometry within the S1/S1' subpocket, despite maintaining hydrophobic character. Although the aromatic ring of phenylalanine can form favorable π-interactions with indinavir, the substantial increase in side-chain volume (~50 Å³) forces unfavorable repositioning or compression of the inhibitor at its closest contact point (2.4 Å), disrupting optimal van der Waals packing that stabilizes the wild-type complex. The modest energetic cost reflects a balance between lost favorable contacts from the bulky substitution and partial compensation through new aromatic interactions, resulting in net destabilization of the inhibitor complex.
